$comment: Single source of truth for every Buildd cron trigger. An external scheduler (cron-job.org) calls these with `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`. vercel.json declares NO crons: the Vercel-native mechanism does not fire in this project, and routes parked there silently never ran. Run `bun run cron:plan` to preview, `bun run cron:sync` to apply, `bun run cron:check` as a CI gate. Schedules are 5-field cron expressions evaluated in `timezone`. Reconciliation is origin-scoped: only jobs under CRON_TARGET_BASE_URL + /api/cron/ are ever touched, so unrelated projects sharing the scheduler account are safe. `scripts/cron-coverage.test.ts` enforces that every /api/cron/* route appears here exactly once. See docs/cron-jobs.md and docs/specs/external-cron-triggers.md.

jobs.$comment: Mission/task schedule tick. Hourly, on the hour, all 24 hours. Cadence floor is the finest ENABLED task_schedules row: every one is now hourly-or-coarser, so */30 bought nothing and woke Neon 48x/day instead of 24x. Hour field MUST stay `*` even though nightly is otherwise off — an hour range here is what silently starved every schedule for 12h a night, and an enabled schedule fires at 06:00. Before making this coarser than a row's cadence, check: isOverdue() allows only interval*2 before flagging a schedule late.
jobs.title: Buildd: Schedules Tick

jobs.$comment: BT-11/BT-19 stall notification. Route comment recommends every 5 minutes. Staged dark — no trigger has ever existed for this route.
jobs.title: Buildd: Stall Notify

jobs.$comment: Distills feedback down-votes/dismissals into memories. Runs every 4 hours. Enabled once the write-type/read-filter mismatch (type=decision vs type=pattern) was fixed in PR that introduced this.
jobs.title: Buildd: Feedback Digest

jobs.$comment: Weekly signing-key rotation (cross-app-assertion-grant spec B.3). Rotates when the Active key is older than 30d, so a weekly tick is sufficient. Staged dark — no trigger has ever existed, meaning signing keys have never rotated.
jobs.title: Buildd: JWKS Rotation

jobs.$comment: Aggregates 7 days of task outcomes for model-routing calibration. Read-only; weekly is enough since the window is 7d. Staged dark — no trigger has ever existed for this route.
jobs.title: Buildd: Routing Calibration

jobs.$comment: Refreshes expiring Codex/Claude/MCP-connector OAuth credentials and verifies Claude liveness. Moved off Vercel-native cron: it never fired there, so an MCP connector credential holding a valid refresh token stayed dead for 15 days until a manual reconnect. Cadence is load-bearing — apps/web/src/lib/cron-cadence.ts derives the credential sweep's lookahead window from this expression, so changing it here changes the window. Deliberately NOT restricted to daytime: OAuth tokens expire overnight too, and the sweep window is derived from an EVEN interval — an hour-restricted schedule leaves an 8h night gap the 5h window cannot cover, which is the exact bug this whole change fixed. 6 runs/day is a negligible share of Neon wake time next to the */30 schedules tick.
jobs.title: Buildd: Credential Refresh

jobs.$comment: Reminds about connector-blocked tasks and proactively alerts on expired/unrefreshable connector credentials. POST. Moved off Vercel-native cron, which never fired — the expiry alert added in #1837 could not have worked there. Cadence */5 * * * * -> hourly: a sub-hourly DB-touching job never lets Neon's compute autosuspend, so it bills idle time all day. Daytime only (EST): nothing here needs to fire while nobody is awake to act on a push. (was 0 * * * *)
jobs.title: Buildd: Connector Block + Expiry Notify

jobs.$comment: Queue-stall watchdog. Alerts when a task has been pending past the route's 4h threshold and was never successfully claimed, naming the claim gate that is holding it. Threshold and cadence are chosen together: the incident this fixes took 5 DAYS to notice, so the target is 'same working day', and hourly x 4h threshold makes worst-case detection ~5h. Daytime only (EST) for the same reason as the other DB-touching jobs — a sub-hourly job never lets Neon's compute autosuspend, and nobody can act on a stalled-queue push at 03:00; a stall that begins overnight is reported at 07:00. Do NOT make this finer than hourly: the route HTTP-probes connectors for role-gated tasks.
jobs.title: Buildd: Queue Stall Watchdog

jobs.$comment: Releases expired credential leases and alerts the owning team. Moved off the Vercel-native cron (never fired); enabled after review — its first run acts on a full accumulated backlog, once. Cadence */10 * * * * -> hourly: a sub-hourly DB-touching job never lets Neon's compute autosuspend, so it bills idle time all day. Daytime only (EST): a stale lease overnight costs nothing but a delayed release. (was 0 * * * *)
jobs.title: Buildd: Lease Expiry Guard

jobs.$comment: Redis-gated fast tick for the SAME route as the hourly guard above, which stays the unconditional floor. Reads one sorted set (buildd:due:lease-expiry, written by /api/runner/credential-lease on acquire/heartbeat/release) and returns without querying Postgres unless a lease has actually lapsed — so */5 costs 288 Redis reads a day and zero extra Neon wake time. Why it needs to be this fast: the lease TTL is 5 minutes and the broker renews every 60s, so hourly detection was 12x coarser than the state it watches. Fail-open by design: if Redis is unconfigured or erroring the gate proceeds to the DB, because 'I could not ask' must never read as 'nothing to do'. See apps/web/src/lib/cron-due-queue.ts and docs/design/cron-wake-windows.md.
jobs.title: Buildd: Lease Expiry Guard (gated)

jobs.$comment: Heals workers whose PR merged on GitHub but whose row still says otherwise — a missed pull_request webhook delivery starves every dependent task until this corrects it, so the cadence has to be within the working hour, not the working day. Merge-state only: the dead-zone sweep (which spawns conflict-resolution tasks) stays on the daily job below. The sweep is capped and rate-limited per run, so a backlog drains across runs. Offset off :00 to stay clear of the schedules tick, but only by 10 minutes: Neon autosuspends after ~5 idle minutes, so a far-away offset opens a second wake window every hour for no benefit. Routes here cap at 60s.
jobs.title: Buildd: PR Merge-State Sweep

jobs.$comment: Full PR reconcile: merge-state plus the dead-zone sweep, which CREATES conflict-resolution tasks and therefore stays daily. Moved off the Vercel-native cron (never fired); enabled after review — its first run acts on a full accumulated backlog, once. Moved off 02:00 into the working day (EST). (was 0 2 * * *)
jobs.title: Buildd: PR Reconcile

jobs.$comment: Weekly archive of completed tasks. Moved off the Vercel-native cron (never fired); enabled after review — its first run acts on a full accumulated backlog, once. Moved off 06:00 into the working day (EST). (was 0 6 * * 1)
jobs.title: Buildd: Task Archive

jobs.$comment: Reclaims workers stuck in waiting_input (mission tasks 4h, standalone 24h) across ALL accounts. Exists because the sweep's only automatic driver was each runner's own 30-minute cleanup timer, and the sweep is now correctly account-scoped — so an account whose runners are all down had nothing to reclaim its stuck workers, which is precisely the case the timeout exists for. A runner-driven trigger cannot be the only trigger for a timeout about runners being unavailable. Hourly x the 4h floor puts worst-case detection ~5h, well inside the threshold's own tolerance. Do NOT make this sub-hourly: it is a DB-touching housekeeping sweep, and sub-hourly work never lets Neon's compute autosuspend. Daytime only (EST): the sweep FAILS a worker and CREATES a retry task, and a retry task queued at 03:00 needs a runner to claim it — the accounts this cron is for are exactly the ones with no live runner, so firing overnight buys nothing and the 8h night gap adds at most 8h to a wait that is already 4h+ by construction. Offset to :15 — clear of the schedules tick at :00 and the merge-state sweep at :10, while still inside the wake window they already opened. Spacing crons far apart buys nothing but idle compute. ENABLED on first ship, deliberately: there is no accumulated backlog to detonate — the pre-fix sweep ran GLOBALLY on every runner's tick, so every account's past-threshold waiting_input worker has already been reaped by whichever runner ticked last. The only rows this can find are ones that accrued after the scoping fix, and each is bounded by the same 4h/24h thresholds that were already in force.
jobs.title: Buildd: Waiting-Input Reclaim Sweep

jobs.$comment: Two jobs in one route: (a) post-deploy health watch — probes the verificationUrl of every release that recently reached `healthy` and transitions it to `degraded` (auto-filing a workspace task) on non-2xx; (b) stale-`deploying` sweep — retries verification, then hard-fails to a terminal state. Cadence */2 -> hourly: both DB queries run unconditionally on every tick, so at */2 this single job kept Neon's compute awake 24/7 by itself (720 wakes/day) — the exact cost the other jobs here are spaced out to avoid. The watch window is NOT hardcoded against this number: apps/web/src/lib/cron-cadence.ts derives it from this expression (interval × LOOKAHEAD_SAFETY_FACTOR), so retuning here retunes the window and no release falls in the gap. Accepted tradeoff: degradation detection latency goes ~2min -> <=~1h; minute-granularity prod alerting belongs in uptime monitoring, not in a Neon-touching cron. Must stay an EVEN interval (all 24 hours, no `7-23` range): cronIntervalMinutes() throws on hour-restricted forms because their real gap is the 8h overnight one, and releases are cut at any hour. Offset to :05, NOT :50: Neon autosuspends after ~5 idle minutes, so a tick 50 minutes away from the :00 cluster opens a SECOND wake window every hour, while :05 lands inside the one the schedules tick already opened. Every route here caps at 60s, so 5 minutes is clear of a collision with room to spare. Spacing crons far apart costs wake time; spacing them a few minutes apart costs nothing.
jobs.title: Buildd: Release Health Check
